target.statement: For the fixed operational data declared below, establish the conjunction that (i) the two-sided contextual relation is the coarsest response-compatible congruence and its quotient has the terminal finer-to-coarser universal property and finite minimum cardinality over the raw quotient map; (ii) under compact-metrizable continuity and quotient-map hypotheses this quotient is compact metrizable with continuous multiplication and response; (iii) finite normalized typed local-kernel replacement supports a compact right-override soft protocol monoid and the retained mediator target face of the released BSC pair has unequal exact total-variation diameters despite the same passive law; (iv) independent randomized hard protocols form an affine convolution monoid whose released BSC contextual signatures have full rank, so equal passive laws do not determine the randomized response experiment under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphism; (v) declared finite standard-Borel DAG kernels give Borel protocol responses and the compact-Polish jointly Feller right-override tier gives a compact metrizable operational quotient; and (vi) in the category that fixes the mediator parameter experiment and circle heat geometry, the circle heat-kernel pair has the same passive retained law but strict one-way Blackwell comparison and strict soft response-set inclusion. No canonical raw latent/DAG realization, target-erasing arbitrary-soft result, correlated-randomization result, uncontrolled regular-conditional identification, noncompact topological quotient theorem, VFE/ELBO emergence, agency, gauge/RG extension, or ontology claim is in the target.
target.quantifiers: For every monoid A, response set Y, and response map Phi:A->Y, the algebraic contextual-quotient conjunct is universal. For every compact metrizable monoid A with jointly continuous multiplication, metrizable Hausdorff Y, and continuous Phi, and every continuous response-compatible quotient triple (q,B,psi) whose surjection q is a quotient map, the compact-quotient conjunct is universal. For every finite DAG presentation with finite state spaces and declared compact typed palettes of normalized local replacement kernels, the normalized soft-replacement semantics is universal; the unequal target-face diameters are asserted for the specified BSC models L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4), every epsilon with 0<epsilon<1/2, and every interior pair epsilon<s_-<s_+<1-epsilon. For the released fifteen-class hard BSC monoids and independently randomized selectors, the affine-convolution and full-contextual-rank conjunct is asserted at passive crossover delta=5/12 under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms. For every finite standard-Borel DAG with standard-Borel protocol palettes and declared jointly evaluation-measurable normalized pointwise kernel families, the Borel-response conjunct is universal; for every compact-Polish jointly Feller instance whose protocol monoid is the finite right-override product of compact metrizable palettes and isolated bottom symbols, the compact operational quotient conjunct is universal. For the circle heat-kernel models and every 0<s<t, the passive-equality, strict one-way Blackwell, and strict soft-response-set conjunct is universal in s and t, with a positive smooth strictness witness for every 0<rho<t-s. Every experiment comparison preserves the declared target/type coloring, response codomain, mediator parameter experiment, circle heat geometry where applicable, and admitted morphism class.
domains: Arbitrary monoids A with identity, arbitrary response sets Y, and maps Phi:A->Y for the probability-free contextual quotient.

Compact metrizable monoids with jointly continuous multiplication and continuous responses into metrizable Hausdorff spaces, together with continuous response-compatible quotient triples (q,B,psi) whose surjection q is a quotient map, for the topological quotient.

Finite DAG presentations with finite standard-Borel node spaces, normalized baseline kernels, compact typed palettes J_v of normalized replacement kernels, one isolated bottom_v symbol per node, and the finite coordinatewise right-override product A=product_v({bottom_v} disjoint-union J_v).
The released fifteen-class hard intervention monoids for the BSC chains L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4), their probability simplices, and independently sampled sequential selectors.

Finite DAGs on declared standard-Borel spaces with standard-Borel protocol palettes and declared jointly evaluation-measurable normalized pointwise baseline and replacement-kernel families; and the compact-Polish jointly Feller sub-tier with compact metrizable palettes, isolated bottom symbols, and finite coordinatewise right override.

The circle T with normalized Haar probability m and positive smooth heat kernels H_t for 0<s<t, with the mediator parameter experiment and circle heat geometry fixed or transformed only by explicitly response-intertwining heat-geometry-preserving relabelings.
codomains: The syntactic response quotient Syn(Phi), its descended response, and continuous compact realizations through countable contextual signatures when the compact hypotheses hold.

Retained probability laws with total-variation geometry, affine randomized response experiments, and P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra in the standard-Borel tier or weak-law topology in the compact-Polish Feller tier.
Circle probability laws and mediator-to-output Markov experiments ordered by heat-geometry-preserving Blackwell garbling.
target.regularity: Algebraic quotient claims require only total monoid multiplication. Compact claims require compact metrizability, joint continuity of multiplication, Hausdorff response codomain, response continuity, and quotient-map factorization; compact-to-Hausdorff continuous surjections supply the quotient-map condition. Finite soft and randomized claims use normalized kernels and finite sums. Standard-Borel claims use standard-Borel palettes, explicitly declared normalized kernels with joint evaluation measurability, P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra, and finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion. The positive compact tier additionally requires compact Polish node spaces, compact metrizable replacement palettes, isolated bottom symbols, jointly continuous finite right-override multiplication, and jointly Feller kernels. Heat kernels are the standard positive smooth Feller convolution kernels on the circle. No topology on an arbitrary all-kernel space and no pointwise version inferred from observational conditionals is assumed.
measures: Normalized laws on each finite or standard-Borel node space and the retained-variable product sigma-algebra.
Probability measures on each finite hard protocol set for independently randomized selectors, composed by convolution.
Normalized Haar probability on the circle and its heat-kernel transition probabilities.
Evaluation sigma-algebra on P(X_ret) in the standard-Borel tier and weak probability-law topology only in the compact-Polish Feller tier.
boundary_conditions: Finite soft preparations use epsilon in (0,1/2); for every epsilon<s_-<s_+<1-epsilon the target-face witness is strictly interior and has separation |1-2b|(s_+-s_-), so it does not rely on hard endpoints.
The mediator target/type face is retained in the finite soft comparison; target-erasing morphisms are outside the theorem.

Randomized sequential selectors are independent and unmarked, response is affine, and admitted isomorphisms are response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms; correlated or shared-noise selection is outside the theorem.
The statement that boundary point interventions span the full retained simplex is restricted to the declared four-atom witness, whose four boundary point interventions are its four vertices.
Standard-Borel point interventions use declared pointwise mechanisms; arbitrary observational regular-conditionals at null conditioning values are outside the theorem.
Compactness, finite right-override multiplication, and Feller continuity are additional sufficient hypotheses, not consequences of standard Borelness; no noncompact quotient regularity is asserted.
The circle comparison fixes the mediator parameter experiment and heat geometry; strict soft inclusion uses a positive smooth preparation H_rho with 0<rho<t-s.
Response-law equivalence does not assert equality of fixed-observation ELBOs, latent posteriors, or generative factorizations.
symmetries: Monoid isomorphisms are unital and response preserving; continuous variants are continuous and respect the quotient triples, and randomized variants are affine convolution-monoid maps.
Typed relabelings preserve node targets, replacement palettes, response codomain, and total variation on the marked mediator face.
The circle comparison fixes the mediator parameter experiment; any admitted relabeling preserves the circle heat geometry and explicitly intertwines every retained response.
Bare response-monoid automorphisms are not quotiented away when the raw quotient map from A is part of the universal-property data.
target.equivalence: Algebraic contextual equivalence is a equiv_Phi b exactly when Phi(uav)=Phi(ubv) for all u,v in A. Response-compatible quotient triples are compared over A by maps commuting with quotient maps and descended responses; continuous triples require q to be a quotient map. Probability responses are equal as normalized measures, kernels are equal pointwise as declared model data or almost surely under their explicit conditioning law, finite target faces are compared by typed total-variation-preserving relabelings, randomized experiments by response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms, and circle experiments by mediator-parameter-preserving Markov garblings or explicitly response-intertwining heat-geometry-preserving relabelings.
premises: The released hard-intervention and canonical-selection packages at repository revision 53cafa374a668ea017a7c50ddbeb75e9045f73a8 supply the fixed BSC presentations and fifteen hard protocol classes but do not supply the new proofs.
The contextual quotient retains the raw protocol monoid A, response map Phi, response codomain Y, declared target/type coloring where present, and admitted morphism class as fixed operational data.

Finite local replacement uses A=product_v({bottom_v} disjoint-union J_v) with compact metrizable J_v, isolated bottom_v, and coordinatewise right override, where bottom_v means leave the declared mechanism unchanged; this finite-product multiplication is jointly continuous.
The randomized protocol monoid uses independent convolution on the finite hard monoid and the response of a selector law is the affine mixture of deterministic responses.
The Borel tier uses standard-Borel palettes, joint evaluation measurability, P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra, and finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion.
The circle heat semigroup is typed by H_s H_t=H_(s+t) and acts on Fourier modes by H_t e_n=exp(-n^2 t)e_n; the comparison category fixes this heat geometry and retained mediator parameter experiment.

No premise supplies a canonical raw latent realization, a target-erasing comparison category, shared-noise randomization, a noncompact classifier, an uncontrolled null conditional version, an ELBO identity, an autonomous agent, gauge/RG dynamics, or physical ontology.
permitted_theorems: Elementary monoid-congruence and quotient universal-property arguments, with direction and quotient-map compatibility proved directly in the package.

Compactness and metrizability of countable products of compact metrizable images; compact-to-Hausdorff continuous bijection; product and quotient-map descent; and continuity of finite coordinatewise right override with isolated bottom symbols, all with hypotheses mapped directly.

Finite-DAG kernel normalization, finite affine convolution, exact rational determinant elimination, total-variation invariance under typed bijections, and the extreme-point theorem for affine simplex bijections.
Finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion for declared standard-Borel kernels and continuity of iterated Feller integration on compact Polish spaces.
The circle heat-semigroup law, Fourier diagonalization, and contraction of Markov operators on bounded Fourier modes, each derived or mapped explicitly.

Blackwell comparison as existence of a response-side Markov garbling in the fixed mediator parameter experiment. Exact recomputation may corroborate finite identities but cannot close a mathematical claim.
target.falsification_criterion: A counterexample within any conjunct's frozen hypotheses, a failure of the stated universal-property factorization or uniqueness over A, a failure of the quotient-map or jointly continuous right-override hypotheses to support descent, a singular contextual-signature minor at the declared BSC parameters, an admitted reverse Markov garbling of H_s through H_t for some 0<s<t, or a normalization, measurability, continuity, response-intertwining, or target-preservation gap refutes the affirmative conjunction. Failure of any explicitly excluded raw-realization, target-erasing, correlated, null-version, noncompact, VFE/ELBO, agency, gauge/RG, or ontology extension does not refute this target because those claims are outside closure.
